title: Synchronous class-group runtime host
objective: Expose one coarse synchronous class-group service boundary to ordinary compiled Python, install a lazy authenticated native Node host with bounded lifecycle, and preserve typed unavailable/resource/cancellation/corrupt-result failures

oracles: Production service protocol and injectable runtime-host differential tests

handoff.summary: Added the CPython-parseable runtime.class_group_backend().call boundary and a lazy synchronous Node facade over the canonical resident JSONL service. The host authenticates packaged artifacts, bounds files/requests/responses/timeouts, validates canonical envelopes and decimal bindings, owns restart-safe generations, kills native process groups on retirement, rejects unsafe Python integers, and reports a typed Windows Wasm fallback. Focused tests cover lazy startup, resident reuse, compiled-Python calls, teardown, corrupt output, missing service, restart-stale bindings, and exactness rejection.
risks: The full build reaches and publishes the updated compiler/runtime caches but fails in the unrelated numerical reactor stage because the checked production manifest has a different toolchain identity.
The broad compiler suite cannot load the optional packages/flint/build/Release/sagejs_flint.node in this worktree; all nine failures have that same missing-addon cause.
next_steps: Re-run pnpm build, pnpm test:compiler, and pnpm test:integration in the integration worktree after its native FLINT and numerical reactor artifacts are reconciled.
Exercise the authenticated platform-package receipt path once the packaging lane is merged.
